core_sources.title: Qualitative Research in Sociology: An Introduction
core_sources.coverage: Qualitative foundations; positivism and constructionism; structured, unstructured, active and focus-group interviewing; ethnography, autoethnography and institutional ethnography; visual sociology; grounded theory, qualitative content analysis, narrative analysis, conversation analysis and discourse analysis; writing; ethics.
core_sources.authority: Introductory disciplinary methods text. Strong for mapping sociological traditions and basic distinctions; dated for digital methods, contemporary critical methodologies and generative-AI governance.
core_sources.limitations: Introductory compression sometimes treats broad families as more unified than later method-specific literature allows; some technical guidance predates contemporary digital research and reporting standards.

core_sources.title: Ethnography: Principles in Practice
core_sources.coverage: Reflexive ethnography; research design, cases and samples; access; field relations; interviews; documents and artefacts; digital ethnography; recording, organizing and analysing data; writing; ethics.
core_sources.authority: Longstanding specialist ethnography text combining philosophical argument, field practice and extensive exemplars. Particularly authoritative for reflexivity, progressive focusing and the relation between fieldwork and analysis.
core_sources.limitations: Defends a recognizable ethnographic tradition and is sceptical of some novelty claims; therefore it should not be treated as neutral on postqualitative, decolonial or radically experimental ethnographies.

core_sources.authors: Kathleen deMarrais, Kathryn Roulston, and Janie Copple
core_sources.title: Qualitative Research Design and Methods: An Introduction
core_sources.coverage: Qualitative foundations, ethics, theory and design; interview studies; participant observation and ethnography; documents and archives; narrative inquiry; autoethnography; arts-based research; quality and trustworthiness.
core_sources.authority: Current, pedagogically explicit qualitative-design text that centres ethics, positionality and theory-method alignment. Useful as a contemporary baseline rather than a specialist manual for every methodology.
core_sources.limitations: Introductory and selective; it explicitly does not claim encyclopaedic coverage. Some quality techniques are presented through Lincoln and Guba traditions that remain debated across methodologies.

core_sources.authors: Norman K. Denzin, Yvonna S. Lincoln, Michael D. Giardina, and Gaile S. Cannella (eds.)
core_sources.title: The SAGE Handbook of Qualitative Research
core_sources.coverage: History and paradigms; ethics and regulation; feminist, critical-race, intersectional, queer, disability, Indigenous, postcolonial, poststructural and new-materialist inquiry; interviews and observation; ethnography; situational analysis; thematic analysis; netnography; autoethnography; performance and arts-based inquiry; communicative methodology; evidence, co-production, impact and futures; foundational chapters on case study, focus groups, triangulation, writing and postqualitative research.
core_sources.locations: Chs. 1-34, pp. 1-652; ebook foundation chapters 35-44; especially Ch. 15 interviews, p. 317; Ch. 16 observation, p. 333; Ch. 17 ethnography, p. 351; Ch. 18 situational analysis, p. 369; Ch. 19 thematic analysis, p. 385; Ch. 20 netnography, p. 403; Ch. 21 autoethnography, p. 421; foundation chapters 40-44.
core_sources.authority: Major pluralist handbook representing multiple interpretive communities and current critical debates. Strong for preserving paradigm disagreement and documenting newer methodological developments.
core_sources.limitations: An edited, explicitly political and pluralist intervention rather than a single coherent methodology. Chapters differ in evidential style, ontology and practical specificity; propositions cannot be generalized across the volume without chapter-level attribution.

core_sources.authors: Boris H. J. M. Brummans, Bryan C. Taylor, and Anu Sivunen (eds.)
core_sources.title: The SAGE Handbook of Qualitative Research in Organizational Communication
core_sources.coverage: Organizational qualitative approaches: mixed research, ethnography, rhetoric, pragmatism, phenomenology, communicative constitution, feminist, critical-race/intersectional, postcolonial, queer, ethnography of communication, autoethnography and engaged scholarship; design, access, interviews/focus groups, participatory, digital and visual data; PIQDA, narrative, rhetorical, conversation, ventriloquial, sociomaterial/affective, critical-discourse, digital-work, tension/paradox and process-ontology analyses; representation and digital forensics.
core_sources.locations: Part I, pp. 3-258; Part II, pp. 261-378; Part III, pp. 381-586; Part IV, pp. 589-661; afterwords, pp. 664-680.
core_sources.authority: Current field-specific handbook that connects general qualitative methodology to organizational communication, access constraints, digital work and specialized analytic traditions.
core_sources.limitations: Discipline-specific. Some named approaches are best understood as field traditions or analytic sensibilities rather than standardized methodologies; transfer to other disciplines requires justification.

core_sources.authors: Matthew B. Miles, A. Michael Huberman, and Johnny Saldana
core_sources.title: Qualitative Data Analysis: A Methods Sourcebook
core_sources.coverage: Design, case definition, sampling, instruments, mixed methods and data management; ethics; first- and second-cycle coding and memoing; within- and cross-case analysis; matrices and networks; methods for exploring, describing, ordering, explaining and predicting; conclusion drawing and verification; quality, auditability and writing.
core_sources.locations: Part I, Chs. 1-4; Part II, Chs. 5-10; Part III, Chs. 11-13. Especially Ch. 4 coding; Chs. 5-10 displays; Ch. 11 conclusion verification and negative evidence.
core_sources.authority: Seminal practical sourcebook for systematic, display-based qualitative analysis. Strong for traceable analytic operations, comparison, rival explanations and cross-case reasoning.
core_sources.limitations: Its realist and partly postpositivist analytic orientation is not methodologically neutral. Some procedures conflict with reflexive, poststructural or anti-coding approaches if imported without epistemological justification.

core_sources.authors: Paul Hague, Nick Hague, and Carol-Ann Morgan
core_sources.title: Market Research in Practice: A Guide to the Basics
core_sources.coverage: Market-research planning; desk research; focus groups; depth interviewing; observation; sampling; face-to-face, telephone and self-completion surveys; data analysis, reporting and research-industry ethics.
core_sources.locations: Ch. 1 Introduction; Ch. 2 design; Ch. 3 desk research; Ch. 4 focus groups, pp. 48-59; Ch. 5 depth interviewing, pp. 60-72; Ch. 6 observation; Ch. 7 sampling; Chs. 9-11 survey modes; later chapters on analysis, reporting and ethics.
core_sources.authority: Practice-oriented market-research manual, valuable for commissioning, logistics, client decisions and mixed qualitative-quantitative sequencing.
core_sources.limitations: Treats qualitative work primarily as diagnostic/exploratory input for managerial decisions and often contrasts understanding with population measurement. It is not an adequate authority for interpretive epistemology or critical qualitative methodology.

core_sources.authors: Joseph F. Hair Jr., Arthur H. Money, Phillip Samouel, and Mike Page
core_sources.title: Research Methods for Business
core_sources.coverage: Business-research process, ethics, problem formulation and literature review; secondary data; research design and sampling; primary data collection; measurement, scaling and questionnaires; qualitative and quantitative analysis; hypothesis testing, correlation, regression and reporting.
core_sources.locations: Whole-volume business-research sequence; qualitative methods and analysis situated within design, primary-data collection and analytic chapters.
core_sources.authority: Integrated business-methods textbook useful for problem-method alignment and the relation between qualitative and quantitative evidence in managerial research.
core_sources.limitations: Broad introductory scope; qualitative traditions are compressed and often positioned within a managerial decision framework rather than developed as distinct epistemological methodologies.

core_sources.authors: Donald R. Cooper and Pamela S. Schindler
core_sources.title: Business Research Methods
core_sources.coverage: Business-research process and ethics; exploratory, descriptive and causal designs; qualitative research; observation, surveys and experiments; measurement; sampling; data preparation and analysis; reporting and presentation.
core_sources.locations: Qualitative exploration in the design and data-collection parts; survey, observation and experimental chapters; analysis and reporting sections.
core_sources.authority: Established business-research textbook with strong design, measurement and managerial-decision orientation.
core_sources.limitations: The qualitative material is embedded in a broader empirical-business framework and should not be treated as definitive on method-specific interpretive standards.

core_sources.authors: William G. Zikmund, Barry J. Babin, Jon C. Carr, and Mitch Griffin
core_sources.title: Business Research Methods
core_sources.identifier: Edition and publisher supplied in the volume; file metadata gives 2012 copyright.
core_sources.coverage: Business problem definition; exploratory, descriptive and causal research; qualitative orientations including phenomenology, ethnography, grounded theory and case study; focus groups, depth interviews and conversation; observation; surveys and experiments; sampling, measurement, quantitative analysis and reporting.
core_sources.locations: Part on research design; Ch. 7 qualitative research; Ch. 9 survey overview; Ch. 11 observation; Ch. 12 experiments; later sampling, measurement, analysis and reporting chapters.
core_sources.authority: Comprehensive business-research textbook useful for linking research objectives to design families and for comparing qualitative, survey, observational and experimental approaches.
core_sources.limitations: Methodological traditions are translated into a business-research taxonomy. Specialist qualitative standards and paradigm conflicts require supplementation.

external_sources.title: Using thematic analysis in psychology
external_sources.relevance: Foundational thematic-analysis articulation.
external_sources.limitations: Predates later differentiation of reflexive, codebook and coding-reliability thematic analysis.

external_sources.title: One size fits all? What counts as quality practice in (reflexive) thematic analysis?
external_sources.relevance: Differentiates thematic-analysis families and rejects generic quality rules.
external_sources.limitations: Written by proponents of reflexive thematic analysis; not a neutral synthesis of all TA variants.

external_sources.title: To saturate or not to saturate? Questioning data saturation as a useful concept for thematic analysis and sample-size rationales
external_sources.outlet: Qualitative Research in Sport, Exercise and Health, 13(2), 201-216
external_sources.relevance: Method-specific critique of saturation in reflexive TA.
external_sources.limitations: Does not invalidate saturation in all methodologies; argument is explicitly tied to reflexive TA.

external_sources.title: A worked example of Braun and Clarke's approach to reflexive thematic analysis
external_sources.relevance: Transparent worked example of reflexive TA.
external_sources.limitations: Illustrative rather than comparative validation.

external_sources.authors: Kirsti Malterud, Volkert D. Siersma, and Ann D. Guassora
external_sources.title: Sample size in qualitative interview studies: Guided by information power
external_sources.relevance: Alternative to formulaic sample-size and saturation claims.
external_sources.limitations: Primarily framed around qualitative interview studies; information power still requires judgement.

external_sources.authors: Bridget C. O'Brien, Ilene B. Harris, Thomas J. Beckman, Darcy A. Reed, and David A. Cook
external_sources.title: Standards for reporting qualitative research: A synthesis of recommendations
external_sources.relevance: SRQR reporting framework.
external_sources.limitations: Reporting checklist, not a substitute for methodology-specific quality judgement.

external_sources.authors: Allison Tong, Peter Sainsbury, and Jonathan Craig
external_sources.title: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ): A 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups
external_sources.outlet: International Journal for Quality in Health Care, 19(6), 349-357
external_sources.relevance: Interview/focus-group reporting transparency.
external_sources.limitations: Designed for interviews/focus groups in health research; may become ritualistic if treated as universal quality criteria.

external_sources.title: Journal article reporting standards for qualitative primary, qualitative meta-analytic, and mixed methods research in psychology
external_sources.relevance: JARS-Qual and mixed-methods reporting.
external_sources.limitations: Psychology-oriented; standards require adaptation to other disciplines and radical qualitative paradigms.

external_sources.title: Qualitative quality: Eight "big-tent" criteria for excellent qualitative research
external_sources.relevance: Broad quality vocabulary across qualitative traditions.
external_sources.limitations: Big-tent criteria are heuristics, not universally commensurable measures.

external_sources.title: Critical analysis of strategies for determining rigor in qualitative inquiry
external_sources.relevance: Critiques mechanical use of trustworthiness techniques.
external_sources.limitations: Argues from a particular conception of methodological coherence; not all paradigms share its assumptions.

external_sources.authors: Linda Birt, Suzanne Scott, Debbie Cavers, Christine Campbell, and Fiona Walter
external_sources.title: Member checking: A tool to enhance trustworthiness or merely a nod to validation?
external_sources.relevance: Qualifies member checking as contextual and dialogic.
external_sources.limitations: Health-research emphasis; participant disagreement does not mechanically arbitrate truth.

external_sources.title: Quality in Qualitative Research
external_sources.relevance: Nuanced treatment of quality, validity and methodological craft.
external_sources.limitations: Predates current digital and AI-assisted research; broad rather than method-specific.

external_sources.title: Intercoder reliability in qualitative research: Debates and practical guidelines
external_sources.relevance: Explains when and how intercoder reliability may be useful.
external_sources.limitations: ICR remains inappropriate for reflexive and some interpretive approaches; agreement does not establish interpretive validity.

external_sources.authors: James A. Holstein and Jaber F. Gubrium
external_sources.title: The Active Interview
external_sources.relevance: Interview accounts as actively co-produced rather than mined from passive respondents.
external_sources.limitations: A constructionist model; not all interview traditions accept its strongest ontological implications.

external_sources.title: Qualitative interviews in psychology: Problems and possibilities
external_sources.relevance: Shows how interview interaction and reporting conventions can be analytically consequential.
external_sources.limitations: Conversation-analytic/discursive orientation is not the only legitimate use of interviews.

external_sources.title: Qualitative research: Introducing focus groups
external_sources.relevance: Focus-group interaction as a source of data, not just multiple simultaneous answers.
external_sources.limitations: Brief primer; does not cover contemporary online or culturally specific focus-group designs.

external_sources.title: Focus Groups in Health Research: Exploring the Meanings of Health and Illness
external_sources.relevance: Shows how focus-group interaction generates access to participants’ meanings and the co-construction of accounts.
external_sources.limitations: Uses health-research examples and a constructionist/feminist argument; applicability depends on research purpose, group composition and analytic unit.

external_sources.title: Ethnography in/of the world system: The emergence of multi-sited ethnography
external_sources.relevance: Extends ethnography beyond bounded single sites.
external_sources.limitations: Multi-sited breadth can weaken depth if following strategies are not theoretically disciplined.

external_sources.authors: Sarah Pink, Heather Horst, John Postill, Larissa Hjorth, Tania Lewis, and Jo Tacchi
external_sources.title: Digital Ethnography: Principles and Practice
external_sources.relevance: Digital ethnography as more than transferring old techniques online.
external_sources.limitations: Broad principles require platform-, population- and jurisdiction-specific ethical adaptation.

external_sources.title: Ethnography for the Internet: Embedded, Embodied and Everyday
external_sources.relevance: Internet use as embedded, embodied and everyday.
external_sources.limitations: Specific platform ecologies have changed rapidly since publication.

external_sources.title: Patchwork ethnography
external_sources.relevance: Challenges uninterrupted long-term immersion as the sole legitimate ethnographic temporal form.
external_sources.limitations: Patchwork must not become a label for under-resourced or thin fieldwork without adequate relational depth.

external_sources.title: Internet Research: Ethical Guidelines 3.0
external_sources.relevance: Context-sensitive ethics for internet-mediated research.
external_sources.limitations: Advisory rather than jurisdictionally binding; requires local legal and institutional review.

external_sources.authors: Gunther Eysenbach and James E. Till
external_sources.title: Ethical issues in qualitative research on internet communities
external_sources.relevance: Public availability does not settle ethical expectations of privacy.
external_sources.limitations: Technologically dated; the contextual principle remains relevant.

external_sources.title: Critical questions for big data
external_sources.relevance: Scale, access and trace data do not eliminate interpretation or ethics.
external_sources.limitations: Addresses big-data discourse broadly rather than qualitative digital ethnography alone.

external_sources.title: Five misunderstandings about case-study research
external_sources.relevance: Clarifies case knowledge, generalization and falsification.
external_sources.limitations: Advocates case-study value but does not resolve all design differences among Stake, Yin and Eisenhardt traditions.

external_sources.title: Building theories from case study research
external_sources.relevance: Comparative case selection and theory-building in organization research.
external_sources.limitations: Postpositivist theory-building orientation differs from intrinsic/interpretive case study.

external_sources.authors: Kathleen M. Eisenhardt and Melissa E. Graebner
external_sources.title: Theory building from cases: Opportunities and challenges
external_sources.relevance: Case-theory relation and transparency in management research.
external_sources.limitations: Field-specific and theory-building oriented.

external_sources.title: The Art of Case Study Research
external_sources.relevance: Interpretive, intrinsic and instrumental case study.
external_sources.limitations: Less procedural than Yin-style design; not aimed at statistical or replication logic.

external_sources.title: Case Study Research and Applications: Design and Methods
external_sources.relevance: Case-study design, propositions, evidence and analytic generalization.
external_sources.limitations: Realist/design-control orientation is not shared by all interpretive case-study traditions.

external_sources.authors: Barney G. Glaser and Anselm L. Strauss
external_sources.title: The Discovery of Grounded Theory: Strategies for Qualitative Research
external_sources.relevance: Original grounded-theory strategies and theoretical sampling.
external_sources.limitations: Later Glaserian, Straussian, constructivist and situational-analysis branches diverge substantially.

external_sources.title: Constructing Grounded Theory
external_sources.relevance: Constructivist grounded theory, reflexivity and co-construction.
external_sources.limitations: One grounded-theory tradition; its epistemology is not interchangeable with Glaserian objectivism.

external_sources.title: Basics of Qualitative Research: Techniques and Procedures for Developing Grounded Theory
external_sources.relevance: Systematic grounded-theory procedures.
external_sources.limitations: Can be applied mechanistically; differs from both Glaserian and constructivist variants.

external_sources.authors: Adele E. Clarke, Carrie Friese, and Rachel Washburn
external_sources.title: Situational Analysis: Grounded Theory After the Interpretive Turn
external_sources.relevance: Situational, social-worlds/arenas and positional mapping.
external_sources.limitations: Not simply an optional diagramming step within conventional grounded theory; it carries distinct theoretical commitments.

external_sources.authors: Hsiu-Fang Hsieh and Sarah E. Shannon
external_sources.title: Three approaches to qualitative content analysis
external_sources.relevance: Conventional, directed and summative qualitative content analysis.
external_sources.limitations: Health-research framing; the three-way typology does not exhaust all content-analysis traditions.

external_sources.authors: Ulla H. Graneheim and Berit Lundman
external_sources.title: Qualitative content analysis in nursing research: Concepts, procedures and measures to achieve trustworthiness
external_sources.relevance: Meaning units, condensation, codes, categories and themes.
external_sources.limitations: Nursing context; category/theme terminology varies elsewhere.

external_sources.title: The qualitative content analysis process
external_sources.relevance: Preparation, organizing and reporting phases.
external_sources.limitations: Procedural clarity can conceal interpretive judgement if used as a recipe.

external_sources.title: Qualitative Content Analysis in Practice
external_sources.relevance: Systematic coding-frame construction and revision.
external_sources.limitations: Coding-frame orientation may not fit highly reflexive or post-coding designs.

external_sources.authors: Nicola K. Gale, Gemma Heath, Elaine Cameron, Sabina Rashid, and Sabi Redwood
external_sources.title: Using the framework method for the analysis of qualitative data in multi-disciplinary health research
external_sources.relevance: Matrix-based framework method for case-and-code comparison.
external_sources.limitations: Not suitable for every epistemology or every data form; requires experienced interpretive leadership.

external_sources.title: Narrative Methods for the Human Sciences
external_sources.relevance: Thematic, structural, dialogic/performance and visual narrative analysis.
external_sources.limitations: Narrative methods remain heterogeneous; no single sequence applies to all.

external_sources.authors: D. Jean Clandinin and F. Michael Connelly
external_sources.title: Narrative Inquiry: Experience and Story in Qualitative Research
external_sources.relevance: Narrative inquiry as relational, temporal, social and place-based.
external_sources.limitations: Distinct from narrative analysis of bounded texts; not a generic label for all story data.

external_sources.title: Why narrative?
external_sources.relevance: Small stories, narrative practice and cautions against narrative imperialism.
external_sources.limitations: A programmatic intervention rather than a full procedural manual.

external_sources.authors: Harvey Sacks, Emanuel A. Schegloff, and Gail Jefferson
external_sources.title: A simplest systematics for the organization of turn-taking for conversation
external_sources.relevance: Foundational conversation-analysis account of turn-taking.
external_sources.limitations: Not a complete guide to contemporary multimodal or institutional CA.

external_sources.title: Sequence Organization in Interaction: A Primer in Conversation Analysis I
external_sources.relevance: Sequential analysis and next-turn proof procedure.
external_sources.limitations: Specialist and data-intensive; cannot be reduced to ordinary thematic coding of transcripts.

external_sources.authors: Charles Antaki, Michael Billig, Derek Edwards, and Jonathan Potter
external_sources.title: Discourse Analysis Means Doing Analysis: A Critique of Six Analytic Shortcomings
external_sources.relevance: Distinguishes discourse analysis from quotation, summary and under-analysis.
external_sources.limitations: Discursive-psychology orientation; discourse traditions differ.

external_sources.title: Critical Discourse Analysis: The Critical Study of Language
external_sources.relevance: Text, discursive practice and social practice in critical discourse analysis.
external_sources.limitations: One CDA tradition; critics dispute explanatory scope and analyst authority.

external_sources.title: The theory, practice, and evaluation of the phenomenological method as a qualitative research procedure
external_sources.relevance: Descriptive phenomenological reduction and meaning structure.
external_sources.limitations: Not interchangeable with hermeneutic phenomenology or IPA.

external_sources.authors: Jonathan A. Smith, Paul Flowers, and Michael Larkin
external_sources.title: Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis: Theory, Method and Research
external_sources.relevance: Idiographic IPA and double hermeneutic.
external_sources.limitations: IPA is a distinct methodology and should not stand in for all phenomenology.

external_sources.title: Phenomenology of Practice: Meaning-Giving Methods in Phenomenological Research and Writing
external_sources.relevance: Phenomenological writing and interpretation of lived meaning.
external_sources.limitations: Hermeneutic orientation conflicts with purely descriptive claims.

external_sources.title: Analytic autoethnography
external_sources.relevance: Analytic autoethnography and theoretical elaboration.
external_sources.limitations: Contested by evocative autoethnographers.

external_sources.authors: Carolyn Ellis and Arthur P. Bochner
external_sources.title: Analyzing analytic autoethnography: An autopsy
external_sources.relevance: Defends evocative, relational and aesthetic autoethnography against analytic domestication.
external_sources.limitations: Programmatic polemic; does not settle evaluation across all autoethnographic genres.

external_sources.title: Talking about pictures: A case for photo elicitation
external_sources.relevance: Photo elicitation and expanded interview cognition.
external_sources.limitations: Photographs do not carry self-evident meanings; image production and interpretation require analysis.

external_sources.authors: Caroline Wang and Mary Ann Burris
external_sources.title: Photovoice: Concept, methodology, and use for participatory needs assessment
external_sources.relevance: Participant-generated photography, dialogue and policy engagement.
external_sources.limitations: Empowerment is not automatic; ownership, safety, visual consent and dissemination power remain contested.

external_sources.title: Document analysis as a qualitative research method
external_sources.relevance: Systematic document review and triangulation.
external_sources.limitations: Documents must be treated as produced and used social artefacts, not neutral repositories.

external_sources.title: Method Meets Art: Arts-Based Research Practice
external_sources.relevance: Arts-based design, analysis, representation and evaluation.
external_sources.limitations: Arts-based research is internally diverse; aesthetic success and research quality are related but not identical.

external_sources.authors: J. Gary Knowles and Ardra L. Cole (eds.)
external_sources.title: Handbook of the Arts in Qualitative Research
external_sources.relevance: Range of arts-informed methods and representations.
external_sources.limitations: Edited plurality; no single quality standard applies to all arts practices.

external_sources.authors: Michael D. Fetters, Leslie A. Curry, and John W. Creswell
external_sources.title: Achieving Integration in Mixed Methods Designs—Principles and Practices
external_sources.relevance: Integration through design, methods, interpretation and reporting.
external_sources.limitations: Health-services framing; philosophical compatibility still requires study-specific justification.

external_sources.title: Mixing qualitative and quantitative methods: Triangulation in action
external_sources.relevance: Classic mixed-method triangulation in organization research.
external_sources.limitations: Early convergence framing has been substantially qualified by later literature emphasizing complementarity and divergence.

external_sources.title: What is participatory research?
external_sources.relevance: Participation defined by shifts in power and control, not merely techniques.
external_sources.limitations: Broad typology; contemporary co-production and Indigenous governance require further specificity.

external_sources.title: Participation: The New Tyranny?
external_sources.relevance: Power capture, depoliticization and token participation.
external_sources.limitations: Critical diagnosis does not imply that all participatory research is invalid.

external_sources.title: Decolonizing Methodologies: Research and Indigenous Peoples
external_sources.relevance: Colonial histories of research and Indigenous research agendas.
external_sources.limitations: Cannot be reduced to a generic checklist or metaphor for methodological novelty.

external_sources.title: Indigenous Methodologies: Characteristics, Conversations, and Contexts
external_sources.relevance: Relational, contextual and community-accountable Indigenous methodologies.
external_sources.limitations: Indigenous methodologies are nation-, community- and protocol-specific; pan-Indigenous generalization is hazardous.

external_sources.authors: Eve Tuck and K. Wayne Yang
external_sources.title: Decolonization is not a metaphor
external_sources.relevance: Warns against converting decolonization into a broad metaphor detached from land and sovereignty.
external_sources.limitations: Not a procedural methods manual; its political claim must be situated geographically.

external_sources.title: Slavery is a Metaphor: A Critical Commentary on Eve Tuck and K. Wayne Yang’s “Decolonization is Not a Metaphor”
external_sources.relevance: Complicates decolonial discourse and historical analogy.
external_sources.limitations: Theoretical intervention, not direct procedural guidance.

external_sources.title: When Black + lesbian + woman != Black lesbian woman: The methodological challenges of qualitative and quantitative intersectionality research
external_sources.relevance: Rejects additive treatment of intersecting identities and identifies design/analysis challenges.
external_sources.limitations: Focused empirical context; intersectionality traditions are diverse and politically situated.

external_sources.title: Exploring the use of artificial intelligence for qualitative data analysis: The case of ChatGPT
external_sources.relevance: Direct comparison of AI querying with prior human analyses.
external_sources.limitations: Two post-hoc datasets, one model generation, no blinded parallel teams; stronger on descriptive than subtle interpretive themes.

external_sources.title: Query-based analysis: A strategy for analyzing qualitative data using ChatGPT
external_sources.relevance: Three-step query-based analysis as an alternative to coding-first workflows.
external_sources.limitations: First published online in 2025; a proposed method, not established consensus; model and interface dependence.

external_sources.authors: Julia Wachinger, Till Barnighausen, Lena N. Schafer, Kerry Scott, and Shannon A. McMahon
external_sources.title: Prompts, pearls, imperfections: Comparing ChatGPT and a human researcher in qualitative data analysis
external_sources.relevance: Empirical comparison of AI and human coding/analysis.
external_sources.limitations: Limited dataset and task; descriptive overlap cannot establish epistemological equivalence or broad reliability.

external_sources.authors: Rudolf Messner, Samuel Smith, and Carol Richards
external_sources.title: Artificial intelligence and qualitative data analysis: Epistemological incongruences and the future of the human experience
external_sources.relevance: Tests human-only against human-AI analysis and foregrounds empirical-boundary and epistemological problems.
external_sources.limitations: One empirical project and model configuration; authors advance a strong constructivist-human-experience position.

external_sources.title: Generative AI in qualitative research and related transparency problems: A novel heuristic for disclosing uses of AI
external_sources.relevance: TROUT-AI disclosure heuristic across team, interaction, design, data and analysis.
external_sources.limitations: Conceptual framework first published online in late 2025; requires empirical validation and does not decide whether AI should be used.

external_sources.authors: Vimukthi Jayawardene and Michael T. Ewing
external_sources.title: Generative AI-augmented thematic analysis
external_sources.relevance: GAATA workflow using multiple tools, prompts and human validation.
external_sources.limitations: Online-first 2025 and issue 2026; marketing-context demonstration; its use of agreement statistics conflicts with reflexive-TA assumptions and requires independent replication.
